A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same image–DNA–taxonomy alignment work, renamed from BIOSCAN-CLIP to CLIBD. All 16 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original BIOSCAN-1M retrieval experiments, INSECT zero-shot classification results, and modality and batch-size analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on both datasets, including revised classification results, additional ablations and four-seed training variability.

M1.justification: v1 trains the encoders through LoRA and fixes the contrastive temperature at 0.07. v2 uses full fine-tuning and learns the temperature initialized at 0.07 (Section 3.1; Appendix C). This substantially changes the optimized parameters, while retaining the encoder families, symmetric trimodal contrastive loss and nearest-neighbor retrieval framework.

E1.justification: BIOSCAN-1M and INSECT remain the experimental datasets; BIOSCAN-5M is discussed without being evaluated. Retrieval-scenario coverage narrows slightly: v1 Table 9 evaluates DNA queries against image references, whereas v2 reports DNA queries only against DNA references. Image-query classification and the seen/unseen-species tasks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds explicit majority/chance baselines in Table 7 and OpenCLIP-based image/text encoder comparisons in Table 11. The principal existing comparators—BioCLIP, BZSL, CNN DNA encoder, DNABERT-2 and BarcodeBERT—remain, so this is a targeted extension rather than wholesale replacement.

E3.justification: Main training changes from 15 epochs, batch size 800 and learning rate 0.001 to 50 epochs, batch size 2000, a one-cycle schedule spanning 1e-6 to 5e-5, and AMP. BioCLIP and threshold-based IS+DU evaluations move from validation to test, while thresholds remain tuned on validation; v1 already contained test retrieval results. Figure 2 also revises reported seen test-query/key counts from 6878/6530 to 4878/6350 despite retaining the Appendix A partitioning rule.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's modality, key-type and batch-size studies, v2 adds encoder/prealignment comparisons, temperature, AMP and LoRA-versus-full-fine-tuning ablations (Tables 11 and 14–16). It adds attention success/failure cases and compares UMAP embeddings across alignment configurations. The batch-size study is revised, while the averaged-image/DNA-key analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v1 provides no training-run variability reporting. v2 Appendix B.1 and Figure 9 newly report four random-seed training runs for the full trimodal model, with means and shaded uncertainty across retrieval settings and taxonomic levels. The uncertainty definition remains ambiguous: the text says standard deviation, while the caption says standard error.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and supplemented. For example, reported test-set species image-to-image macro harmonic mean for I+D+T changes from 32.4% in v1 Table 8 to 51.2% in v2 Table 1; the best aligned-encoder INSECT harmonic mean changes from 38.1% to 35.0% (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 4). These concern revised training/settings, not controlled cross-version gains or losses. New ablation results appear, while DNA-to-image and averaged-key entries disappear.

T1.justification: The symmetric contrastive-loss equations and trimodal sum remain mathematically equivalent. However, v2 removes v1 Section 3.1's explicit LoRA weight factorization and parameter-count argument, retaining only an empirical LoRA comparison. This is a limited reduction in mathematical method detail; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of contrastively aligning images, DNA and taxonomy for seen/unseen species classification remain. The abstract reduces the claimed zero-shot accuracy advantage from over 11% to over 8%. The introduction and conclusion more explicitly foreground DNA as a better alignment target than taxonomic text when labels are scarce.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking DNA's advantage to sparse species labels, attention patterns to successful insect recognition, and encoder prealignment to image-to-text performance. It argues that simple classifiers can make BZSL's complexity unnecessary and discusses accuracy–resource tradeoffs. The conclusion newly makes the two-dataset and CLIP-style-training limitations explicit, alongside the persistent cross-modal performance gap.

D1.justification: Implementation reporting expands substantially: v2 specifies bfloat16 AMP, the learning-rate schedule, alternative encoder checkpoints, attention-rollout blocks 2–6, and measured memory use and training times. Reported hardware changes from two to four 80GB A100 GPUs. Appendix A adds detailed class-overlap and sample statistics, while the earlier LoRA projection and parameter-count details are omitted.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes the broad fine-grained multimodal survey, including discussions of methods such as ImageBind, BLIP and CLOOB, and refocuses positioning on biological classification, DNA representations and label scarcity. New cited work includes MycoAI, BIOSCAN-5M and environmental-DNA/remote-sensing research. The BioCLIP publication update refers to the same retained work.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming BIOSCAN-CLIP to CLIBD, v2 substantially rewrites the introduction, related work and experimental narrative. It creates a dedicated analysis subsection, consolidates cross-modal/BZSL discussion, moves classifier details into Appendix B.2, and organizes implementation ablations in a new Appendix C.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column layout and extensively restructures tables around query/key combinations, separating macro and micro results. Retrieval examples become a combined three-mode display, UMAP expands from one plot to four panels, and attention and uncertainty figures are added. The split and class-distribution diagrams are also revised.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility: threshold-based IS+DU results are evaluated on test data rather than the validation set used for tuning, four-seed reporting addresses previously undocumented variability, and controlled ablations support important training choices. Added failure cases and explicit limitations improve interpretation. Removed retrieval analyses and reporting inconsistencies, particularly Figure 9's standard-deviation/standard-error ambiguity, temper these gains, but the stronger validation and supporting evidence establish a substantial net improvement.
